name: install Homebrew into ~/.homebrew
purpose: Isolated Homebrew -- never /opt/homebrew or /usr/local, no sudo required

name: load Homebrew into this shell
purpose: Puts brew on PATH for every step below (stow, mise, brew bundle)

name: install stow and mise
purpose: Bootstrap dependencies -- everything else is pinned by mise. Declares its state because `brew install` exits 1 when any formula's post-install hook flakes (a cosmetic cert symlink, say) even though every requested formula installed; Homebrew has one failure code for that and for a genuinely missing formula, so only the resulting state can tell them apart. The state names the isolated prefix rather than asking PATH: a `stow` belonging to another account's Homebrew must not count as this step having succeeded

name: install Nix (single-user)
purpose: Linux's counterpart to the isolated Homebrew above. Single-user: /nix is created once with sudo and then owned outright by this account, so every package operation afterwards is unprivileged. --no-channel-add because the package set comes from the flake, not from a channel; --no-modify-profile because ~/.zshrc is a stow symlink into this repository and the installer would otherwise append its snippet straight into the tracked file -- packages/linux/.zprofile.d/45-nix.zsh sources nix.sh instead

name: load Nix into this shell
purpose: Puts nix on PATH (and NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE in the environment) for the build step below. The counterpart to `brew shellenv` on macOS

name: build the pinned Nix environment
purpose: Realises manifests/linux/flake.nix -- stow, mise, zsh, git and tree, at the exact nixpkgs revision in flake.lock. --extra-experimental-features on the command line rather than from ~/.config/nix/nix.conf: that file is stowed, and stow has not run yet (it comes from this very build). The out-link doubles as the GC root, so nix-collect-garbage cannot delete the environment out from under a live shell

name: load the Nix environment into this shell
purpose: Makes stow and mise resolvable for the steps below, the same way the Homebrew shellenv step does on macOS

name: stow the platform package set
purpose: Deploys packages/{common,unix,<platform>} into $HOME. Goes through stow-packages.sh rather than calling stow directly so that bootstrap and reapply share one definition of the package set and one guard against deploying another platform's package; that script also creates the real target directories first, so stow links managed files individually instead of folding a stateful directory such as ~/.pi into the repository

name: install pinned tools (mise)
purpose: CLI tools and language runtimes are pinned to exact versions in packages/common/.config/mise/config.toml; neither Homebrew nor a nixpkgs revision pins them per-tool. Must run after the stow step, which links that file into $HOME where mise reads it. Deliberately not OS-gated: the whole point of the split is that both machines get the same tool versions

name: install Brewfile packages
purpose: Only what mise cannot pin: bootstrap deps, formulae with no mise backend, the docker CLI plugins, and casks. Runs after mise so a failure here cannot leave the pinned toolchain uninstalled. Linux's equivalent is manifests/linux/flake.nix, built above

name: wire docker CLI plugins
purpose: docker resolves buildx/compose from ~/.docker/cli-plugins, not PATH -- installing the formulae is not enough. macOS only: the plugins are Homebrew formulae, and on Linux docker's own packaging already puts them where the CLI looks

name: register herdr plugins
purpose: Herdr reads a plugin registry it keeps in ~/.config/herdr/plugins.json rather than scanning its plugin directory, and that registry holds absolute paths this repo cannot track. Stowing a plugin's files therefore leaves Herdr unaware of it. Runs after stow, which places the files, and after mise, which installs herdr itself

name: register the pinned zsh as a valid login shell
purpose: chsh refuses a shell that is not listed in /etc/shells. macOS needs no equivalent: zsh is already the default login shell there, which is why this whole pair is Linux-only. Skipped unless $HOME is genuinely this account's home directory: `sudo chsh` acts on the ACCOUNT, not on $HOME, so a run against a throwaway $HOME is NOT sandboxed -- one did exactly that and repointed the real login shell at a path under /tmp, which would have locked the account out of every new shell once that directory was cleaned up

name: make the pinned zsh this account's login shell
purpose: Everything this repository configures lives in .zprofile/.zprofile.d/.zshrc, so on a distribution that defaults to bash the entire deployment is inert until the login shell is zsh -- the tools are installed and simply never reach PATH. Run through sudo rather than bare `chsh` so it does not prompt for a password. Note this points the login shell at the Nix out-link: if that link is ever deleted, new shells fail to start -- see the recovery one-liner in the README.
